title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: The Latest Transfer Out Through Telephone, Online or Mobile Banking
content:
This page belongs to the Savings & Money Market Accounts rules on bringing an inactive account back to life through the customer's own transfer out. It fixes which posting supplies the point in time that reactivation carries.

## Rule

Only three ways of moving money out of the account matter here: telephone banking, online banking, mobile app transfers. Branch cash, ATM cash, ACH pulls, checks, wires, internal transfers or any other outflow: none of these counts.

For each of the three channels, take its most recent posting of a transfer out; a channel with no such posting at all contributes nothing. The latest of those postings, across all three channels, is taken as the transfer the customer carries out in the contact, so its posting is the reactivation's point in time.

## Illustration (hypothetical account history)

| Channel | Most recent posting of a transfer out |
|---|---|
| Telephone banking | 20 January |
| Online banking | 2 April |
| Mobile app | 14 March |

The latest of the three is 2 April, so that online banking transfer supplies the reactivation's point in time.

## Points to weigh

**If only one of the three channels ever saw a transfer out, what then?** Its most recent posting is the latest by itself.

**Is branch cash taken out at a later point relevant?** No. Branch cash lies apart from the three channels, whatever its timing.
